EN: <Companion Protocol::Return Base>

Speaker: Raul
Topic_Name: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.
EN: Hey, as long as you're not asking me to go back to Black Mountain, I'm a happy old man.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.
EN: It is. We'll meet up at the Lucky 38.

Speaker: Rex
Topic_Name: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.
EN: {confirmation bark}<bark!>

Speaker: Cass
Topic_Name: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.
EN: {Wary, doesn't like 38}All right... don't be long. {Under her breath}Robots there give me the creeps.

Speaker: Cass
Topic_Name: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.
EN: {Wary, doesn't like 38}All right. Guess Vegas it is.

Speaker: Cass
Topic_Name: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.
EN: {Wary, doesn't like 38}Back to the gilded cage.

Speaker: Lily
Topic_Name: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.
EN: Nice children shouldn't stay in places like that, dearie! That's the sort of place Leo likes! But if you insist....

Speaker: Pretty Sarah
Topic_Name: You're not one of the merchandise?
EN: Most of my body is scarred all over, like a ghoul. Nobody around who'd want to screw that. No, I just run things.

Speaker: Scrambler
Topic_Name: How did you all break out?
EN: Dynamite. Lots and lots of dynamite. You should've seen the body parts flying everywhere.

Speaker: Scrambler
Topic_Name: What did you do to end up in here?
EN: Not much, just killed a bunch of people. Maybe a couple of kids, too. Whatever.

Speaker: Scrambler
EN: That's right. Fuck off.

Speaker: Scrambler
EN: Why? It's because I mess up people so bad they don't know what part goes where when I'm done.

Speaker: Meyers
Topic_Name: Does that mean you'll take the law into your own hands?
EN: When I need to, yes.

Speaker: Meyers
Topic_Name: I'll need to think about it.
EN: Understood.

Speaker: Meyers
EN: All right, then. Guess I'll just make a quiet exit - no need for a goodbye party or anything.

Speaker: Meyers
Topic_Name: How would you feel about becoming Primm's new sheriff?
EN: Assuming an NCR pardon comes with the job - and it had better - I'll also need to be able to do things my own way.

Speaker: Meyers
Topic_Name: How would you feel about becoming Primm's new sheriff?
EN: Due process has its place, but sometimes it's just a waste of time. I'll need to know that I'm not going to end up right back in prison.

Speaker: Meyers
Topic_Name: How would you feel about becoming Primm's new sheriff?
EN: My terms are the same. A pardon from the NCR and the freedom to do the job anyway I see fit.

Speaker: Eddie
EN: {dismissive, slightly unfriendly}Yeah, get out of here.

Speaker: Caesar
Topic_Name: You should probably be talking to somebody else.
EN: Answer the question.

Speaker: Caesar
EN: You need to work on your bloodthirst. We won't speak again until Benny is dead.

Speaker: Caesar
EN: Walk away if you want, but if you do, he's going up on a cross. You're still making a choice.

Speaker: Caesar
EN: What's wrong with you? This man shot you, stole from you, left you in the desert to die.

Speaker: Caesar
EN: Consider it the first of many {slight emphasis, you know your using a fancy word}bestowments.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: We had packed the old city with C4 and dynamite. Crude, but it did the job. Those who didn't die in the blast were in no position to mount a defense.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: The ones left on the dam didn't know what to do. The troopers routed them. Graham pulled the remaining legionaries back, but the battle was over.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: He went south, back to the Grand Canyon, back to Caesar. And that was the last we saw or heard from Joshua Graham.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Caused total chaos among the younger legionaries, and Oliver's troopers fell back to the side walkways and stayed out of the veterans' way.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: By the time the veterans got to the ridge, we were already in Boulder City.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: They followed us down there, but we were out before they realized what was happening.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: But once they were in, they were stuck there. Oliver's troopers were entrenched and wouldn't give a foot.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: That's when we ordered the rangers and 1st recon sharpshooters to start picking off veteran legion officers from a high ridge west of the dam.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: That only lasted about a minute before Graham ordered the back ranks to push through to the front and rush the ridge.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Joshua Graham, Caesar's old legate, he's wasn't so flexible.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: When the Legion attacked Hoover Dam, General Oliver ordered his troopers back to the middle ground just after first contact.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Graham pushed all of the legionaries onto the dam, filling the east side with recruits up front and veterans in the back, by the book.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: I told him we would take them back into NCR territory because we had already lost ten rangers on the way out. Ten rangers, five men with .308 rifles.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Well, that was enough for them. They packed up what they could and we took them back north. Last I heard, they settled somewhere in {ahn-zah}Anza-{boh-reh-goh}Borrego.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Raised Bighorners. Had some tough times, but it worked out okay for them. So there you go. That's my one bit of good.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: They had planted an NCR flag over the well and they would not budge until every last one of them was laid out, dead and cold.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: So I walked up and told them there was a group of raiders coming, one hundred strong. {laughing a bit}I made up some cockamamie name for them and everything.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: The men looked at each other, looked at us, and asked me what we were going to do about it.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: There's over two dozen bodies lying in the dunes way outside of town and five men with {three-oh-eight}.308 rifles crouched behind sand bags.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: And these bodies, these people out in the sand, they aren't raiders. Aren't even heavily armed.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: They're just people who were trying to get to the only well in fifty miles. I didn't have to talk to the men to see that they did not care one bit.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Word got back to one of our stations that raiders had been attacking the place. I went out with six rangers.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: We must have been on the trail for a week before we got to Rattletail. We lost one woman to Night Stalkers and another almost died of dehydration.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: When we reach the place, it's six shacks set up around an old well.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: So what happened at Hoover Dam and Boulder City?
EN: In big battles, Caesar deploys his legionaries in waves. Recruits up front, prime soldiers behind the recruits, old guard bringing up the rear.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: So what happened at Hoover Dam and Boulder City?
EN: Opponents wear themselves out dealing with the first two waves, if they survive that long. When the veterans step up, there's not much fight left.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: So what happened at Hoover Dam and Boulder City?
EN: Caesar can adapt, though, and when required, he can run any mix of legionaries as skirmishers and still retain order in the ranks.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Come on. You must have lots of stories.
EN: [FAILED] I do, but I'm tired of telling them. Time changes how you look at things.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: There must be something good the rangers have done that you're proud of.
EN: [SUCCEEDED] It's kind of a long one, but all right. About twenty, twenty-five years ago, a group of NCR settlers pushed way south into Baja.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: There must be something good the rangers have done that you're proud of.
EN: I guess it doesn't seem so far now if you look at a map, but back then, they were out a ways.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: There must be something good the rangers have done that you're proud of.
EN: They built this little shanty town around a well in the middle of nowhere. Called it {rat-ul-tayl}Rattletail.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Sitting on the shore of Lake Mead, looking east. Listening to a radio. Trying to not get too many people killed.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: I'm too old to be slapping leather, but I had hoped for something else. More than this, anyway.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Okay, what are you supposed to be doing?
EN: "To protect against all forms of tyranny." As simple as that. Thirty, forty years ago, the wasteland was full of despots.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Okay, what are you supposed to be doing?
EN: Slavers. Raiders. Tough-talking hoodlums with gangs who liked to kick around towns. Back then the NCR military was still young.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Okay, what are you supposed to be doing?
EN: Couldn't cover much ground. It took groups like ours to tip the balance back to the good guys.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: There's a lot of answers to that question, but it started with the Ranger Unification Treaty. We weren't always the only show in town.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Nevada had its own posse, the Desert Rangers. They fought Caesar even farther east, out in Arizona. Didn't go well for them.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Years back, we met with the Desert Rangers at Mojave Outpost and agreed to help them against Caesar if they would join the NCR.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Well, there's what we're supposed to be doing and what we're actually doing.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: There's a big gap between those two things, about as wide as that lake out there.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How long have you been in the rangers?
EN: Oh, well. I guess it must be coming up on... forty years or so. Back before {eh-leez}Elise was chief, anyway. It was a heck of a lot harder then.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How long have you been in the rangers?
EN: Weren't as many of us to go around. But I think it was a lot easier to tell the good guys from the bad.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Have any good stories to tell?
EN: Suppose it depends on what you think is "good." Most folks want to hear about Hoover Dam and Boulder City, but it's a long story.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Have any good stories to tell?
EN: If you want some tall tales about hunting down slavers or busting up gangs, talk to one of the younger rangers.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Caesar's elite guard. They travel with him wherever he goes. A bit of insurance in case any of his guests get funny ideas.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: They aren't the toughest legionaries, but they're the most devoted to Caesar. They believe in everything the Legion stands for.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: There's no real equivalent to them in the NCR. Centurions are battle-born, elite officers who earned their rank with blood and sweat.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: They wear special outfits, too, pieced together from the armor of all their defeated enemies. Good commanders, tough opponents.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What makes the veterans so tough?
EN: Take a regular legionary and age him ten years. Whatever they lose to age they make up for with experience. Life expectancy isn't long in the Legion.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What makes the veterans so tough?
EN: You live ten years in Caesar's army, you're a force to be reckoned with.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: He wasn't a brilliant strategist. Wasn't tactically flexible, either. There was something about him, though. Menace, indestructibility.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: It made everyone afraid of him. Heck, the praetorians burned Graham four years ago and some of the tribes are still afraid of him.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: They say the Burned Man still walks the land, blackens the earth wherever he sets foot.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: He was a missionary from Utah who hooked up with Caesar at the Grand Canyon, became his translator.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Graham helped Caesar with the Blackfoots after they got captured together. Up until Hoover Dam, he was Caesar's legate.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: You wouldn't think a man of god could turn so brutal. Cruel to his opponents. Did the sort of things that make you sick to talk about.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why do they call Lanius the Monster of the East?
EN: Oh, the usual reasons. People say he's enormous, carries a big sword, chops peoples' heads off. That's not what makes him a good commander, though.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why do they call Lanius the Monster of the East?
EN: Folks say he came from a heck of a tough tribe, took Caesar a long time to conquer. It was thanks to Lanius.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why do they call Lanius the Monster of the East?
EN: But once Caesar broke him, he was born again. He'll go anywhere and do anything to win. Legion says he can smell weakness.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why do they call Lanius the Monster of the East?
EN: Once he finds out where an army's vulnerable, he'll go to it like a dog for the throat.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: I can't say I think the legionaries at Cottonwood deserved the same fate, but what's done is done.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Thanks to you, that's one less pack of slavers for people to worry about.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: By the way, I appreciate what you did for the troopers down there.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Nelson might not be the most strategically important place, but taking Dead Sea out means a lot to them.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Searchlight was worse. One of Caesar's {froo-men-tar-ee}frumentarii must have found something in there, flooded the whole camp with radiation.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Nelson was barely set up. We had a big stretch of unprotected land between Forlorn Hope and Searchlight, and Nelson was the solution.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: A {deh-can-us}decanus named Dead Sea took the place and caused a lot of damage.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Tell me about the heavy troopers.
EN: They have the best equipment the NCR can get its hands on, power armor salvaged from our war with the Brotherhood.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Tell me about the heavy troopers.
EN: Techs strip out the joint servos so you don't need special training to wear it.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Tell me about the heavy troopers.
EN: It feels like you're carrying a Brahmin on your back, but it can take a heck of a lot of punishment.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What do the new rangers mean for NCR?
EN: The Baja rangers can do more advance night scouting and sharpshooting to assist the troopers.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What do the new rangers mean for NCR?
EN: Ranger combat helmets are old Pre-War gear. They have built in low-light optics. Makes a big difference.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Is Moore in charge of all the NCR troopers out here?
EN: No, and thanks to General Oliver for that. Colonel {shoo}Hsu is at McCarran. Most of the New Vegas troopers are under his command.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Is Moore in charge of all the NCR troopers out here?
EN: He's more sympathetic to the locals than Moore, but he's got the Fiends to deal with.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Is Moore in charge of all the NCR troopers out here?
EN: No, and thanks to General Oliver for that.  Colonel {shoo}Hsu is at McCarran. Most of the New Vegas troopers are under his command.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Is Moore in charge of all the NCR troopers out here?
EN: He's more sympathetic to the locals than Moore. Now that the Fiends aren't giving him grief, we should see more troopers assigned to the front lines.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Is Moore in charge of all the NCR troopers out here?
EN: Good work on that, by the way. Hope you got good bounties out of it.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: The colonel is an effective commander - one of the best - but she sharpened her claws on the Vipers and the old Jackals.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Did four tours against the Brotherhood, too. She used to be ranger until an injury took her out of action. Happens to a lot of us, unfortunately.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: She's better at making graves than making friends. Bring in Moore and the earth will be razed. Fields will be salted.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Oh, well... now, you'll have to excuse me. The general and I don't always see eye to eye on things.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Maybe it's best that I just say that he is a trooper, through and through. The man will not give up an inch for anything, least of all to the Legion.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: You've seen it yourself. Some of them don't even have proper service rifles or armor.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Our heavy infantry, power armor units, they're back in NCR territory protecting the interests of Brahmin barons against small-time raiders.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Brahmin barons only have one vote at the ballot box, but they have a lot of money to throw around.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: It's complicated. Goes way back. I told President Kimball that we need more rangers here.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: He accepted that, but took the most experienced ones and sent them south. Patrol rangers are good men and women, but we're about to fight a war.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why are funds tied up at the Boneyard?
EN: Senate elections are coming up. Local representatives don't want to push any more funding to the Mojave campaign because it's unpopular.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why are funds tied up at the Boneyard?
EN: Most of the folks around the Boneyard haven't been to New Vegas and probably never will.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why are funds tied up at the Boneyard?
EN: All they know is that their money gets sucked away to this desert and their brothers, sisters, sons, and daughters die here.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: So that was the end of Graham?
EN: It's not that clear cut. You have to understand, Graham was the toughest son of a gun anyone around these parts had ever seen.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: So that was the end of Graham?
EN: Before Hoover, we had five kill reports on Graham from rangers and 1st Recon sharpshooters who tried to take him out.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: So that was the end of Graham?
EN: Some folks think he's still alive, call him the Burned Man.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Are the Blackfoots part of the Legion?
EN: Yes and no. The Blackfoots don't exist anymore, just like any other tribe that gets swallowed by the Legion.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Are the Blackfoots part of the Legion?
EN: Caesar takes the tribal out of the tribe. Scrapes and burns off tattoos, breaks up families, forces mixed breeding so all the old loyalties die away.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Are the Blackfoots part of the Legion?
EN: The only tribe in the Legion is the Legion. Caesar is their chief, father, and god all rolled into one.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What happened to Graham after Hoover Dam?
EN: Losing the dam was the worst defeat the Legion ever suffered. Graham had been with Caesar since the beginning, but he had to set an example.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What happened to Graham after Hoover Dam?
EN: The praetorians covered Graham in pitch, lit him on fire, and down into the Grand Canyon he went.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How did a Follower wind up becoming Caesar?
EN: Somewhere along the way, he realized he needed to educate the Blackfoots or they were going to get wiped out with the rest of the tribe.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How did a Follower wind up becoming Caesar?
EN: Showed them how to use guns, how to make explosives. Once he taught the Blackfoots a thing or two, they needed him.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How did a Follower wind up becoming Caesar?
EN: And he no longer needed the Followers, NCR, or anyone else. He decided he could remake the tribes of the southwest, whether they wanted it or not.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How did a Follower wind up becoming Caesar?
EN: He became Caesar and Joshua Graham became his legate, his right hand. And that's where Graham stayed until Hoover Dam.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Out to the Grand Canyon. He met a missionary from Utah, a man by the name of Joshua Graham. Graham helped translate for the Followers and the tribes.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: All three of them got nabbed by the Blackfoots down there, back when they were still at war with every other tribe in the southwest.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Legion fires. They burn high wherever the Legion goes.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Caesar's a hard man to figure out, but he always wants you to know when more troops are at your front door.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Doesn't matter. Your time's up, Hanlon.
EN: Well, you got that right.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: You've convinced me. Your secret is safe.
EN: I don't know if you're working for Caesar or if desperation's made me a heck of a lot more persuasive. Either way, this is the right thing to do.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: You've convinced me. Your secret is safe.
EN: Now, I trust we're done discussing this. I'm going to step through that door and pretend like we never had this talk.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Caesar's dead. What more do you need?
EN: {a little angry}The Legion is more than just Caesar! It's got the momentum of thousands of men behind it.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Caesar's dead. What more do you need?
EN: They're not just going to roll off into Arizona if we give them a good shove.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Caesar's dead. The Legion can't hold itself together for five years, much less ten.
EN: It's a gamble either way. Even with Caesar gone, we still might not outlast the Legion. I suppose that's a risk I'll have to take.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Caesar's dead. The Legion can't hold itself together for five years, much less ten.
EN: For our sake, I hope you're right. I guess I should thank you for bringing me to my senses. So... thanks.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Caesar's dead. The Legion can't hold itself together for five years, much less ten.
EN: Now, if you'll excuse me, I'm going to walk out that door and pretend we never had this talk.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Maybe fifty rangers will die on that dam. We lose over a thousand troopers every year. Being here is crazy. Getting out's the only sane thing to do.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What about you and the rangers?
EN: Rangers are volunteers. Every man and woman who signs up is willing to die for the NCR, myself included.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What about you and the rangers?
EN: A lot of this is my fault. It's only right that I stand with them.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What will you do if I don't turn you in?
EN: Oliver can't stand that rangers got credit for victory at Hoover. Whatever I recommend, he does the opposite. I said I wanted them on the ridge.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What will you do if I don't turn you in?
EN: He put them right on the western part of the dam itself. We don't have enough firepower to hold that spot.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What will you do if I don't turn you in?
EN: If the troopers fall back, and they will, the rangers will advance to cover Oliver's retreat. We lose the dam, Oliver and the senate are ruined.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Too bad. I'm turning you in.
EN: Fair enough. You want to do this the right way, go get one of the rangers. Don't worry. I'm not gonna run out on you.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: {pause, quieter}Creating fear and instability among the troopers without causing harm, it's the only thing I could think of to shake things up.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: It took some people getting killed to realize I had gone too far. I had to stop.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Hold on. This is ranger headquarters. There might be a dozen rangers within earshot.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Think twice before you decide to give the old chief a gut full of lead.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What do you think I should do about this?
EN: First thing that comes to mind is to turn me in. But that might not be the best play, all things considered.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What do you think I should do about this?
EN: Even if your heart's in the right place, I reckon it might do a lot more harm than good.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How does spreading false intel help anything?
EN: {exasperated}People back home don't listen. They don't care. Senators, Brahmin barons, folks who are just trying to make it from day to day.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How does spreading false intel help anything?
EN: It's been so many years that people forget about it. Conscription brings in fresh troops to die here every month. Like it's routine.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How does spreading false intel help anything?
EN: {getting more worked up}And even if we hold this dam, what then? Are we going to send the NCR's men and women to die here for another five years? Ten?

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How does spreading false intel help anything?
EN: Patrol the whole length of the Colorado for hundreds of miles? Holding this dam. {pause, downbeat}It'll be the death of us.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Aren't you fighting for the people of New Vegas?
EN: We're fighting on their behalf, but Mr. House and the families are stringing us up, inch by inch.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Aren't you fighting for the people of New Vegas?
EN: They'll drain us dry while we fight and die over this dam. We offered them sanctuary in NCR territory before, but they won't listen.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Aren't you fighting for the people of New Vegas?
EN: Troopers and rangers have been dying here for more than five years while the families sit pretty behind that... damned wall.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: It's never going to end. This fight with Caesar. People back home don't know what these young men and women are in for.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: The Legion is the worst enemy we've ever faced, but we can't stop Caesar here, not without getting a lot of good people killed.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: More than anyone cares to count up. And even if we do stop him, I don't see how we're ever going to be able to pull out.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: But you're inventing your own intelligence reports. I've seen the logs and talked to the rangers.
EN: {smiling a bit}You have, have you? {Beat, more somber}Misdirection. When you're pinned down, outnumbered, and two days from any help, it's just about the best friend you can have.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: But you're inventing your own intelligence reports. I've seen the logs and talked to the rangers.
EN: Misdirection's what's saved me all these years. It's what saved us at Hoover Dam. But it's been five years now and {see-zar's}Caesar's right across that lake.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: But you're inventing your own intelligence reports. I've seen the logs and talked to the rangers.
EN: He's closer now than he ever was before. {bit angry}I was a young man once. I know what it's like to want to fight for your home, but this isn't it.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why don't the ranger stations send the intel directly to the troopers?
EN: Comm rangers might have an incomplete picture of the situation. There's a lot going on out there.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why don't the ranger stations send the intel directly to the troopers?
EN: Intel needs to be coordinated through Golf so we can verify and advise appropriately.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Why don't the ranger stations send the intel directly to the troopers?
EN: Troopers have enough to deal with. We don't want them questioning their intel.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How do you coordinate the intel?
EN: It's a simple system, when it works. Patrol rangers radio intel to ranger stations.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How do you coordinate the intel?
EN: Comm rangers send the intel up the station chain until it reaches Camp Golf.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: How do you coordinate the intel?
EN: Then I or one of the other rangers on duty organize the data, evaluate it, and send information to camps or troopers in the field.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Can you give me any advice?
EN: Well... {thinking}the logical thing to do is to check with the patrol rangers and comm officers. Don't be too discouraged if some things don't match up.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Can you give me any advice?
EN: Different people see different things, and sometimes the meaning gets twisted, lost in static from person to person.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Do you know anything about the problems?
EN: I don't know Technical Sergeant {ray-ess}Reyes, but coordinating intel can be messy sometimes. Things get mixed up, people get confused.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Do you know anything about the problems?
EN: Heck, I get confused and I've been doing this for a long time now. What he - or she - sees as a problem might be standard operating procedure.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: Do you know anything about the problems?
EN: That's not to say Reyes is wrong for being concerned, but it's easy for the sand to get in your eyes out here.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: I know you're the one who's been manipulating intelligence data.
EN: Hold on. If we're going to have this conversation, let's go somewhere more private.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: I know you're the one who's been manipulating intelligence data.
EN: {joking a bit}Don't worry. Not much bite left in this old dog.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: I'm investigating some intel problems for Technical Sergeant Reyes.
EN: Interesting that she would wrangle someone else into sorting out the problem.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: I'm investigating some intel problems for Technical Sergeant Reyes.
EN: But I suppose you're in the right place. A lot of intel comes through here.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: I'm investigating some intel problems for Technical Sergeant Reyes.
EN: This again? All right. What do you want to know?

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: I didn't realize you were in such a hurry.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: I get so used to sitting in this chair and listening to radio reports, sometimes I forget people are getting ready for a war out there.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: I could tell you a lot if you had the time, but at my age I'm not sure which of us would get tired first. What do you want to know?

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: Not too long ago, they took Nelson and Searchlight.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: They've got some camps on the eastern shore of the Colorado, and the monstrosity on the hill across the lake - that's for Caesar.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: Some folks don't believe he's here yet, but you can tell. He's the eye of the storm. It all roils and spins around him.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: You don't have to see the man to see the effect he has.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: Intel says the legate's coming. {lan-ee-us}Lanius. They call him the Monster of the East. If he's half as bad as Graham was, we're in for a heck of a fight.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: With Caesar and a new legate here, the Legion's not going to fall for the same old bag of tricks.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: Word is that the Legion's old timers have shown up, Caesar's veterans from the Red Okie {sen-tur-ee-ah}Centuria and what was the Painted Rock tribe.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: They're the best of the best and the baddest of the bad. Short of a centurion or {pray-tor-ee-an}praetorian, they don't come any tougher.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What's the Legion been up to?
EN: You come across a pack of them, weigh your options carefully.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: It's no secret that we've had better campaigns. Holding this whole length of river isn't easy.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: We're stretched thin and the Long 15 just keeps getting longer. Slow to get supplies. Slower to get reinforcements.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: NCR's senate has got funds tied up at the Boneyard and President Kimball ordered our most experienced rangers to chase ghosts down in Baja.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Even Caesar knows that General Oliver's coming back to Hoover. Colonel Moore's doing a fine job of running things over at the dam.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: In her own way, of course, when she's not trying to wrangle my rangers into helping her.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: But just keeping that dam secure and operational day to day is enough work for one person, never mind building a defense against the Legion.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Mojave Outpost sent word through the stations. The rangers coming up from Baja moved through Dayglow a week ago.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Some of the patrol rangers have reported that Oliver's power armor heavy troopers are starting to reinforce the front lines.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Wish they got here a bit earlier, but that's the senate for you.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What do you know about Caesar?
EN: The best of the best, worst of the worst. He came out of NCR, one of the Followers of the Apocalypse.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What do you know about Caesar?
EN: Like a lot of the Followers, he went out in the wilderness with a partner to try to help those who needed helping.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
Topic_Name: What do you know about Caesar?
EN: Not much different from how the rangers used to be, except with books and medicine instead of guns.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Folks around here call me the chief{han-luhn}, but Hanlon's just fine. The rangers run themselves pretty well, but I try to lend a hand.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Mostly administrative work, helping coordinate intel on the radio. That and keeping an eye on the fires growing across the water.

Speaker: Chavez
EN: Letting you just walk away isn't how it works, I'm afraid.

Speaker: Chavez
EN: [SUCCEEDED] All right. Pickings were getting slim around here anyway.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Eddie's just going to keep chasing you. Quit while you're ahead... and alive.

Speaker: Chavez
EN: [FAILED] Nope, not interested. No caps in letting people walk, you know.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: How about you walk away and I'll do the same? That way it's easy on both of us.

Speaker: Chavez
Topic_Name: I'm not going to let you live.
EN: {Male PC}Get him!

Speaker: Chavez
Topic_Name: I'm not going to let you live.
EN: {Female PC}Get her!

Speaker: Chavez
Topic_Name: {Terrifying Presence}< Cock your head and grin. >
EN: Run!

Speaker: Chavez
Topic_Name: Eddie sent me to deal with you.
EN: That's nothing new. Am I supposed to be impressed?

Speaker: Eddie
Topic_Name: You only want me to deal with Chavez?
EN: Chavez is the ringleader. Without him, his crew will fall apart, and I don't give a shit about those guys.

Speaker: Eddie
Topic_Name: I'll need to think about this.
EN: Fuck you for wasting my time, then.

Speaker: Eddie
EN: Good. Chavez and his boys were last seen south of here. If you're lucky and he's careless, he might still be there.

Speaker: Weather Station Guard
Topic_Name: < Keep holdout weapons. > Sure, here you go.
EN: You are free to leave.

Speaker: Weather Station Guard
EN: {WAH-lay}Vale.

Speaker: Weather Station Guard
EN: You are free to leave.

Speaker: Testacles the Debug Centurion
Topic_Name: Caesar wants to talk to me about being sick.
EN: Done.

Speaker: Testacles the Debug Centurion
EN: The old guy is now in a coma.

Speaker: Lucius
EN: Avenge {KAI-zar}Caesar!

Speaker: Lucius
EN: [SUCCEEDED] I apologize for my rash action. I understand fighting and killing, not healing. I acted out of grief and loyalty.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: The cranial bleeding was too much for a man of his age. A younger man would have lived.

Speaker: Lucius
EN: [FAILED] It's obvious you know as little about medicine as I do. Spare me your excuses.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: There was, uh, internal bleeding and lesions and other problems.

Speaker: Lucius
EN: [SUCCEEDED] What you say is true. I apologize for my rash action - it was out of grief and loyalty. I hope you understand.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Caesar would be dead if I didn't try to help him. How dare you blame me for trying to save his life!

Speaker: Lucius
EN: [FAILED] Save your excuses.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Hey, it totally wasn't my fault that he died. He was old.

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: President Kimball survived the assassination attempt.
EN: Killing Kimball would've struck fear into the NCR. It's unfortunate that you weren't able to take advantage of this opportunity.

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: President Kimball survived the assassination attempt.
EN: We are preparing to move against the Dam, and Legate Lanius has a part for you to play in the battle. Report to him at his camp.

Speaker: Lucius
EN: {triumphant}The loss of morale in the NCR must have been staggering when their leader fell. It's proof that no one is out of the Legion's reach.

Speaker: Lucius
EN: We are preparing to move against the Dam, and Legate Lanius has a part for you to play in the battle. Report to him at his camp.

Speaker: Victor
Topic_Name: No problem, I'll head up by myself.
EN: Come back soon, now!

Speaker: Victor
EN: Oh boy.

Speaker: Victor
EN: The Boss is pretty clear on this. I can't let you in unless you're by your lonesome.

Speaker: Victor
EN: See ya soon!

Speaker: Judah Kreger
EN: We are here as promised. Now let's kick some ass.

Speaker: Yes Man
EN: Okay! Anything else?

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: What? You think this is my fault?
EN: His head exploded, idiot. Of course it's your fault. {to his men}Avenge {KAI-zar}Caesar!

Speaker: Siri
Topic_Name: What do you know about Legate Lanius?
EN: The Legate is not a man to be crossed, especially if you're a woman. That's all I will say about it.

Speaker: Siri
Topic_Name: Tell me about the Burned Man.
EN: A vengeful spirit, some of the more superstitious women claim. He was a great leader of the Legion before he failed {KAI-zar}Caesar.

Speaker: Siri
Topic_Name: Tell me about the Burned Man.
EN: The story says he was set on fire and thrown into the Grand Canyon, but his angry spirit rose from the ashes of his corpse, looking for revenge.

Speaker: Siri
Topic_Name: Tell me about the Burned Man.
EN: Nonsense, probably, but there's no doubt that many in the Legion believe he's still alive somehow.

Speaker: Antony
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Burned Man?
EN: {hiding his fear behind angry denial}He's a story to frighten the younger Legionaries. He's dead - no man, no matter how tough, could survive a fall into the Grand Canyon.

Speaker: Antony
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about Legate Lanius?
EN: It took years for {KAI-zar}Caesar to conquer Lanius' tribe, and {KAI-zar}Caesar showed mercy to the survivors, allowing them to join the Legion.

Speaker: Antony
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about Legate Lanius?
EN: Had the positions been reversed, {KAI-zar}Caesar would be dead. Lanius is called the Monster of the East because he never, ever shows mercy.

Speaker: Otho
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Burned Man?
EN: {Male PC}It's not something we like to speak of. The Burned Man was our greatest warrior, even greater than Legate Lanius, but he failed {KAI-zar}Caesar at the Dam.

Speaker: Otho
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Burned Man?
EN: He's been dead for several years now, but the rumor is that {KAI-zar}Caesar has scouts out looking for him all the same. The Burned Man was a very tough man.

Speaker: Otho
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Burned Man?
EN: {Female PC}Ask someone else, woman.

Speaker: Otho
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about the Legate?
EN: A great warrior. When he was but a recruit, I watched him kill ten men in the arena with his bare hands.

Speaker: Otho
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about the Legate?
EN: He doesn't feel pain and he never, ever shows mercy. If all Legionaries were like him, the Legion would be invincible.

Speaker: Vulpes Inculta
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about the Legate?
EN: {Caesar alive}To call {Lah-nee-OOS}Lanius ferocious would be an understatement. In battle, he seizes the enemy in his jaws and will not let go.

Speaker: Vulpes Inculta
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about the Legate?
EN: He thinks nothing of suffering losses, so long as the enemy suffers more. Though unsubtle, he is not dim. He detects traps, and sets his own.

Speaker: Vulpes Inculta
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about the Legate?
EN: Be glad you will not have to face his judgment... if you are true to {KAI-zar}Caesar.

Speaker: Vulpes Inculta
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about the Legate?
EN: {Caesar dead}{Lah-nee-OOS}Lanius served {KAI-zar}Caesar well, as his greatest battlefield commander.

Speaker: Vulpes Inculta
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about the Legate?
EN: With {Lah-nee-OOS}Lanius at the head of the Legion, however, I doubt he'll have much use for my services. He prefers... direct methods.

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: {Liked+}After everything I've done for the Legion, this one failure condemns me?
EN: {hesitant, knowing player is right}No... I suppose not. You've proved that you're a friend to us many times. I apologize for my temper.

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: I did all I could to save him.
EN: Yet you failed, and you must pay.

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: <Lie> I did all I could to save him.
EN: Yet you failed, and you must pay.

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
EN: You'll regret this!

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
Topic_Name: It's important that I get in there.
EN: It's probably more important that you get out of here alive. If you haven't noticed, there's a battle going on here.

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
Topic_Name: It's important that I get in there.
EN: Now get out of here!

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
EN: Friend or not, no one is allowed in here. Move along!

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: It's okay I'm a friend.

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
EN: All right, but make it quick.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: [Lie] I've been ordered to get something for Colonel Moore, let me in.

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
EN: Damn it all to hell! Let's go!

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: <Lie> Colonel Moore is in trouble! She needs help now!

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
EN: Our instructions were pretty clear. Now you better get your ass out of here.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Don't you have anything better to do right now than guard this door?

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
EN: I warned you!

Speaker: NCR Heavy Trooper
EN: Stop right there, no one is allowed into the control room!

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: If Caesar dies, who takes over the Legion?
EN: Legate Lanius will take Caesar's place at the head of the Legion. The Legate is a fine warrior, and the Legion will do well under his command.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Adios.

Speaker: Chief Hanlon
EN: Shoot.

Speaker: Vulpes Inculta
Topic_Name: Tell me about the Burned Man.
EN: Ah, yes {you know his name}- we are forbidden from speaking his true name. He was a shaman of some kind before he met {KAI-zar}Caesar, a holy man from out of the Utah.

Speaker: Vulpes Inculta
Topic_Name: Tell me about the Burned Man.
EN: The Burned Man proved dangerous, unpredictable, and impossible to kill. He helped {KAI-zar}Caesar form the Legion but almost led it to destruction.

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: Tell me about the Burned Man.
EN: The Burned Man was {KAI-zar's}Caesar's advisor and general when the Legion was originally formed. The Burned Man led us to a disastrous defeat at the Dam.

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: Tell me about the Burned Man.
EN: On {KAI-zar's}Caesar's orders, the Burned Man was covered in pitch by the {pray-TORE-ian}Praetorian Guard, lit on fire, and cast into the Grand Canyon.

Speaker: Lucius
Topic_Name: Tell me about the Burned Man.
EN: {KAI-zar}Caesar has forbidden us from ever speaking his true name again, and so we simply refer to him as the Burned Man.

Speaker: Dale Barton
EN: He's the best the Legion has to offer, or so the Legionaries say. Brute of man, wears a fancy metal mask into battle.

Speaker: Dale Barton
EN: He killed one of my pack Brahmin simply because it was in his way. I knew better than to complain about it, though.

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I destroyed the Brotherhood of Steel's bunker.
EN: You really know how to make a robot happy! Seriously, you just made my day.

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: Forget the Boomers. I want nothing to do with them.
EN: Okay! Who needs artillery support? Not the good guys, that's for sure!

Speaker: Yes Man
EN: Sorry if that was getting boring!

Speaker: Yes Man
EN: If you're tired of a topic, I'm tired of it, too!

Speaker: Yes Man
EN: Whatever you say!

Speaker: Yes Man
EN: You bet!

Speaker: Yes Man
EN: What should we talk about next?

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: It took some doing, but I convinced the White Glove Society to support Caesar's Legion.
EN: You did? That's... that's an unusual approach!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: It took some doing, but I convinced the White Glove Society to support Caesar's Legion.
EN: But I know it makes sense somehow if you're the one doing it! {shrug}The problem is me!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: The White Glove Society needed a little help getting back to basics, that's all.
EN: That's great news! I wish I could visit their casino! They have a refined sense of taste!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: The White Glove Society had a cannibalism problem, but I solved it.
EN: A cannibalism problem? Really? I'm so glad you weren't eaten!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I spoke to Marjorie and Mortimer. I say leave the White Glove Society alone.
EN: Say no more, say no more... if you say they're good, they're good!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I helped the Omertas perfect their plan to slaughter everyone on the Strip.
EN: You'd think it'd be bad for the Strip but... but I guess it must be good!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I helped the Omertas perfect their plan to slaughter everyone on the Strip.
EN: Yeah - take the Strip down a notch or two, right? That'll show it! Okay!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: The Omertas were plotting to destroy the Strip, so I killed the conspirators.
EN: Wow! That is amazing! You are just - a hero! I am serious!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I know enough about the Omertas to know I want them left alone.
EN: You got it! I won't say another word about them!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I've convinced the Brotherhood to support the NCR.
EN: {shocked}Really? That's... {a catastrophe, but keeping spirits bright}well, that's a surprise! They'll really want to blow me up!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I've convinced the Brotherhood to support the NCR.
EN: But maybe dumb machines like me ought to get blown up and scrapped for salvage. Who knows? Not me!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I know the Brotherhood. I want them left alone.
EN: Okay! Consider them forgotten! Along with the projections that predict they'll be our biggest enemy! Forgotten!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I've set the Great Khans on a path of destruction.
EN: Oooh, sounds dramatic! I like it! Wind them up and let them go!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I've set the Great Khans on a path of destruction.
EN: No more Khans! That's great! They're just bad people...

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I convinced the Great Khans to leave the Mojave.
EN: Maybe they'll be devoured by giant scorpions! All sorts of things could happen to them out there!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I've convinced the Great Khans to support the NCR.
EN: {confused}Really? Okay! That sounds fun!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I've convinced the Great Khans to support the NCR.
EN: That's not aiding an enemy! Not when you do it!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: The Great Khans have been wiped out.
EN: Yay, that's great news! You finished what Mr. House and the NCR started! That's got to feel good!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: I've visited the Khans' settlement at Red Rock Canyon. They can be ignored.
EN: If you say so! Consider them filed away under "not to be discussed again!"

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Omertas?
EN: Hmm. I remember that Benny used to pay a receptionist at Gomorrah for information - maybe she knows something!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Omertas?
EN: Just that Benny didn't like them! He talked on and on about how they couldn't be trusted! And this is coming from Benny!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Omertas?
EN: He hated their casino, said it was tacky! And he thought they were up to something, because he said they always are!

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Omertas?
EN: Do you know anything else about the Omertas?

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Omertas?
EN: Whenever you get around to it will be just fine!

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Omertas?
EN: I'll check into the Omertas some more.

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: Some of Mr. House's data said that he'd lost a bunch of Securitron scouts near Hidden Valley!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: Telemetry showed that they'd been attacked with energy weapons! House was pretty sure it was the Brotherhood!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: There must be a bunch of them holed up there! Not a good place for a robot to visit!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: They go around in big suits of power armor, and they have lots of energy weapons! But there's a downside!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: They just have a {beat}thing about technology! They think it should all be theirs! If someone else has it, they get mad!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: All I'm saying is, not much of a chance they'll accept a Vegas that polices itself with robots!

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: What do you know about the Brotherhood of Steel?

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: No rush! Take your time!

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: Where should I look for the Brotherhood of Steel?
EN: I'm not ready to decide what I want to do with the Brotherhood.

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the White Glove Society?
EN: {uncomfortable stating an opinion}From what I understand, they're perfectly delightful! They're cultured, clean, and {ultimate compliment}super-polite!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the White Glove Society?
EN: Benny didn't like them, though! He said they were "creepy."

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the White Glove Society?
EN: Don't hurry on my account! I'm the one with the flexible schedule.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: What do you know about the White Glove Society?
EN: I'll let you know when I'm done evaluating the White Glove Society.

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Boomers?
EN: They must be a really nasty people! I haven't heard a single good thing about them!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Boomers?
EN: They fire artillery on anyone who comes near their settlement at Nellis Air Force Base. Talk about rude!

Speaker: Yes Man
Topic_Name: What do you know about the Boomers?

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What evidence do you have that Mr. House will make a move?

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What evidence do you have that Mr. House will make a move?

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What could Mr. House possibly be up to?

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What if I can convince them not to join the Legion?
EN: Don't fool yourself. I've dealt with enough of these gangs to know that they can't be trusted. Was there anything else?

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: Where should I start looking for them?
EN: As I said, our scouts were some ways west of HELIOS when they disappeared.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What kind of weapons do they use?
EN: Their standard kit seems to be a blade of some sort and light armor. Guns are not uncommon, but are of questionable condition.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What kind of weapons do they use?
EN: While they prefer to use their blades, it's common for them to scavenge better weapons from their enemies and use those.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What kind of weapons do they use?
EN: The men have been told to toss their weapons over the side of the dam if they receive a fatal wound, but I doubt many will remember.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: You mentioned that they were in good shape?
EN: Yes, extremely so. They must use conditioning routines on par with the rangers, or better.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: You mentioned that they were in good shape?
EN: Their soldiers can run near half again as fast as my best men, and close distances with frightening speed. And they're as strong as they are fast.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: You mentioned that they were in good shape?
EN: Their superior physicality makes them extremely dangerous up close, so I've had the men run drills for taking on larger, stronger opponents.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: You mentioned that they were in good shape?
EN: But they've all been instructed to take them down at range, if possible. I've made it clear I don't want any heroes in my squad, just survivors.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What impressed you about their discipline?
EN: I've never once seen a single one of them back down, or disobey an order.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What impressed you about their discipline?
EN: They'll happily charge a fortified position with little more than a sharpened stick if ordered to, and do so without hesitation.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
EN: I can only spare a few more moments. What did you wish to speak about?

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: It's better to be in charge.
EN: Oh, it has its perks, to be sure. I'm free to see that things on a large scale are done my way, and don't have to tolerate any disagreement.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: It's better to be in charge.
EN: Those few people in a position to countermand my orders only care about results, and in that regard I never leave them less than pleased.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
EN: I do, sometimes. There are days I'd give anything to out in the open air, planting explosives and laying down covering fire.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
EN: But here I am, stuck in the same stale office day after day, while other people get to do the actual fighting.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
EN: But enough reminiscing. Did you have other questions?

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: Are you in charge of the NCR around here?
EN: I command the garrison here at the dam, yes, but Colonel {shoo}Hsu over at McCarran is technically in charge of the area's forces.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What do you know about Caesar's Legion?
EN: They're organized, I'll give them that. The few times I've encountered them firsthand, I've been impressed with their discipline.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What do you know about Caesar's Legion?
EN: I've heard they don't allow women in their military, considering them nothing more than breeding stock.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What do you know about Caesar's Legion?
EN: Their men, however, are typically quite large, in phenomenal condition, and prefer close-quarter weapons.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What do you know about Caesar's Legion?
EN: Recent engagements have taught us to fear their shock attacks, so it's a blessing that we seem to have superior firearms.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about Hoover Dam?
EN: It's of immense strategic value to the NCR. Hoover Dam sends enough electricity west to light every city and major settlement.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about Hoover Dam?
EN: It's moderately defensible, with a single point of entry on the east side. To get to the power plants below, the enemy has to cross the entire top.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: What can you tell me about Hoover Dam?
EN: The Legion's tried to cross the water on a few occasions, but slow-moving boats make easy targets for sharpshooters.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: How did you get to be a colonel in the NCR?
EN: I joined up at a young age. Was barely sixteen when I left home and volunteered to be in the military.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: How did you get to be a colonel in the NCR?
EN: Got a few strange looks at first, but those stopped when I got top marks across the board during training, and became an officer at seventeen.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: How did you get to be a colonel in the NCR?
EN: A few years went by, my squad helped take down gangs of raiders here and there, and one day an invitation to join the Rangers arrived.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: How did you get to be a colonel in the NCR?
EN: Those were the best years of my life. Doing something that truly matters, and having the freedom to handle it as you see fit. Then I got injured.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
Topic_Name: How did you get to be a colonel in the NCR?
EN: Everyone was very supportive. I received a promotion to colonel and given greater responsibility, but my days as a Ranger were over.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
EN: I don't have time to discuss all the different aspects of the NCR with you, but if you want it all in a nutshell - the NCR is progress.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
EN: If you wander around the wasteland you'll find all sorts of tribes, villages, and such where people spend most of their time trying to survive.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
EN: The NCR gives its citizens a shot at something more. We have laws, currency, health care, government. All the things that were lost.

Speaker: Colonel Cassandra Moore
EN: It's not perfect, but it's worth protecting, which is why we also have the largest military in existence.

Speaker: Genaro

Speaker: Genaro
Topic_Name: Not until you tell me where you get the food from.

Speaker: Legate Lanius

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: Good, because the Omertas' plan was stopped, Vegas is as strong as ever.

Speaker: Legate Lanius

EN: {Angry}Unless you seek to goad me into a retreat, leaving the battlefield and leaving my honor here to be trampled underfoot by Republic cowards.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> That strength... other Legates didn't see it either, until it was too late.
EN: [SUCCEEDED] {Slightly to himself}We did take the towers easier than expected. I cannot believe even the Republic would overlook such an opening in their defenses.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> That strength... other Legates didn't see it either, until it was too late.
EN: {Rallying}Yet we are at throat of the Great Bear. Victory is at hand.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: <Bluff> That strength... other Legates didn't see it either, until it was too late.
EN: <Bluff> The position of your veterans, using the Dam's intake towers - all as expected.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> That strength... other Legates didn't see it either, until it was too late.
EN: [FAILED] I am not another Legate, and I am not such a fool as Graham, to be painted in pitch and set aflame.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> That strength... other Legates didn't see it either, until it was too late.
EN: If all NCR believes as you do, then this battle is already won.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> I think they believe you'll be tricked as easily... maybe easier.
EN: [SUCCEEDED] {Thinking}Hnh. {Beat}You believe your own words, even if I do not.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> I think they believe you'll be tricked as easily... maybe easier.
EN: {Slightly suspicious}Perhaps NCR has the strength of a cornered animal... it will not be enough to hold this place.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> I think they believe you'll be tricked as easily... maybe easier.
EN: They know nothing of my tactics - or the strength of my forces. They will learn.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: <Bluff> I think they believe you'll be tricked as easily... maybe easier.
EN: <Bluff> NCR has studied you as they did Graham, and the trap is ready for you.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> I think they believe you'll be tricked as easily... maybe easier.
EN: [FAILED] {Contempt}Then they know nothing of me or the Legion's subjugation of the East.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluff> I think they believe you'll be tricked as easily... maybe easier.
EN: And to send you to deceive me... it is you that they have tricked, not I.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluffs> But... history has shown defeat is assured. Uh, yours, that is.
EN: [SUCCEEDED] {Insulted}You dare speak that name? Comparing him to any man of Caesar will only earn you a slow death.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluffs> But... history has shown defeat is assured. Uh, yours, that is.
EN: {Anger building}You think me some lesser man, some other Legate? I am the first of the Legion, and this gate to the West shall be ours this day.

Speaker: Player / Courier
Topic_Name: <Bluffs> But... history has shown defeat is assured. Uh, yours, that is.
EN: <Bluff> Persist and learn what Graham learned at the Dam - and Boulder City.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluffs> But... history has shown defeat is assured. Uh, yours, that is.
EN: [FAILED] {Slight sneer}Those are your final words? They are too weak to even wash the stain of your disgrace this day.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: <Bluffs> But... history has shown defeat is assured. Uh, yours, that is.
EN: Yet if those are the words you wish to be remembered for, then I shall... {beat, disgust, as if "honor is undeserving}*honor* them.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: Nice mask, can't wait to take it as a trophy.
EN: We shall see how brave you are when nailed to the walls of Hoover Dam, your body facing West so you may watch your world die.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: I'm here to kill you. The Legion's advance ends here.
EN: {Respectful, eager}Enough words, then. Let our strength settle this.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: {Caesar dead}What, Caesar giving you orders beyond the grave?
EN: Caesar's will is the will of the Legion. And the West... all beneath the flag of the Great Bear exist to test the strength of the Legion.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: {Caesar dead}What, Caesar giving you orders beyond the grave?
EN: The West shall fall as the East fell, and all the tribes that stretch to the setting sun shall bear the mark of the Legion.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: {Caesar alive}What, Caesar wasn't brave enough to come take the Dam himself?
EN: Caesar's will is made truth through me. I am a hammer against all that defy his rule.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: {Caesar alive}What, Caesar wasn't brave enough to come take the Dam himself?
EN: If you seek to stand against me, you shall fall as the West falls.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: Maybe you're willing to listen to reason.
EN: {Disgust}I see you fight with words, like all beneath the flag of the bear. Let us hope your skill with weapons proves greater.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: If you think you've got any chance of taking Hoover Dam, you're wrong.
EN: {Disdain}Many graves in the East are filled with those who said as much, with braver words, not backed by strength.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: If you think you've got any chance of taking Hoover Dam, you're wrong.
EN: It is Caesar's {emph}will this gate to the West bear the flag of the Legion. {Beat, a little quieter, resolved}Caesar's will shall be done.

Speaker: Mr. House
ActorNotes: [rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema]
Topic_Name: I'll put you back in your tube, good as new.
EN: {rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema}No... ruined everything... exposed... germs... a year of... life, if... at most...

Speaker: Mr. House
ActorNotes: [rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema]
Topic_Name: You won't be able to control anything, but I'll let you live.
EN: {rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema}No! ...Don't disable... cerebral... I'd rather be... killed... just kill... me...

Speaker: Mr. House
ActorNotes: [rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema]
Topic_Name: Time for you to die, Mr. House.
EN: {rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema}May there be... a hell... for you... a Tartarus...  bleak, unending...

Speaker: Mr. House
ActorNotes: [rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema]
Topic_Name: Yes Man needs you out of the way.
EN: {rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema}{bitter, wheezing laugh}Your... vanity project... doomed to fail...

Speaker: Mr. House
ActorNotes: [rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema]
Topic_Name: By Caesar's command, you will die.
EN: {rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema}Slavery... the future of... mankind? What... have you... done?

Speaker: Mr. House
ActorNotes: [rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema]
Topic_Name: The NCR asked me to get rid of you.
EN: {rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema}Those snakes? ...for them? ...you sad, misguided... whore.

Speaker: Mr. House
ActorNotes: [rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema]
EN: {rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema}Fool... to let... personalities... derail future... of mankind? ...Stupid!

Speaker: Mr. House
ActorNotes: [rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema]
EN: {rasping, wheezing voice, like you have emphysema}If personal gain... what you sought... should've done... as asked...

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Aggressive acts on the casino premises will be met with lethal force. Vacate the premises immediately.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Vacate the premises immediately. The casino is off-limits for 24 hours.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Vacate the premises immediately. All Securitrons are at a state of high alert.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Hold on, now, hold on. Just a moment...

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Turn around and leave, and I'll... I won't attack you any further.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Just... stay away from the console. It doesn't do anything...

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: You've come back to kill me this time, I assume?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Ironic, how this turned out. The thousands of hours I spent calculating odds, running projections, planning for every contingency...

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: ...only to be done in by a mail carrier with a grandiosity complex.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Get it over with, will you?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Think you're doing well to have made it this far?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Your chances of breaking through my defenses, they're... minimal, at best!

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Why are you doing this?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: I would've made you wealthy! You could've helped change the world!

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: You're actually going to do this all over again?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Damn it, will you die already?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: You dared come here, after what you did?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: What do you think you're going to do? Fight you way up to the penthouse and assassinate me?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: You came here to finish what you think you started?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: This is nothing compared to what's waiting for you up in the penthouse.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Vegas will still rise again. Your betrayal won't defeat me!

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: The Lucky 38 will be your grave. I'll finish what Benny couldn't get right!

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Cannibalism was strictly forbidden in their contract. If some of them broke that stricture, they deserved whatever punishment you dealt them.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Did you know I killed some White Gloves who were eating their customers?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: {perturbed}No, I was not aware of this.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: Is it really so hard {emphasis}not to engage in cannibalism? My goodness...

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: It's a violation of their contract. I authorize you to deal with them in any way you see fit.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Did you know some of the White Gloves are... eating people again?

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: {not going to deny it}Yes, of course. But refraining from those "dietary practices" is a primary requirement of their contract.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: They've been good to their word. Put together one hell of a resort hotel, too.

Speaker: Mr. House
EN: From what I hear, I'd want to eat at the Gourmand every night... if I were ambulatory.

Speaker: Player / Courier
EN: Were you aware that the White Glove Society used to be cannibals?

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: Why is the terminal on the North wall off-limits?
EN: I recommend following the Securitron's instructions. Its programming is... {beat}strict, and I don't have time to change it.

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: Where does New Vegas get all its electricity?
EN: {stating the obvious}Hoover Dam, of course. A hydroelectric dam?

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: Where does New Vegas get all its electricity?
EN: The NCR had it up and running at 50% capacity within a year of occupying the dam. By treaty, New Vegas receives 5% of its output - more than enough.

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: You do know Caesar is dead, don't you?
EN: By my calculations, his death will affect the shape of the battle for Hoover Dam minimally, if at all.

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: You do know Caesar is dead, don't you?
EN: The Legion's aggression will outlive Caesar. Indeed, they'll try to take the dam as a tribute to his memory.

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: You do know Caesar is dead, don't you?
EN: Given a year, they'd have him deified - but by then the Legion will be breaking down, riven by internal conflicts, a monster consuming itself.

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: You do know Caesar is dead, don't you?
EN: It's irrelevant. In the short term, the Legion is still monster enough that defeating it will make me look powerful indeed.

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: What's the deal with the snowglobe collection?
EN: What of it? I enjoy them. There's something about a little diorama set inside a glass dome that I... {beat}find pleasing.

Speaker: Mr. House
Topic_Name: What's the deal with the snowglobe collection?
EN: If you run across any out in the wastes, turn them in to Jane. She'll compensate you.

Speaker: Legate Lanius
Topic_Name: About time. I was starting to get bored with all this waiting around.
EN: {Angry}As was I... yet I was ordered to await you. Now that you are here, we may act.

Speaker: Red Lucy
ActorNotes: [A hint of sincere emotion shows through her otherwise stoic mask]
EN: {A hint of sincere emotion shows through her otherwise stoic mask}I've come to expect nothing less from you, brave stranger.

Speaker: Red Lucy
EN: Get to your cage and ready your arm.

Speaker: Red Lucy
ActorNotes: [Pauses to judge players' words, quite taken]
Topic_Name: I'll defeat as many as you've got.
EN: {Pauses to judge players' words, quite taken}I can see your resolve, determined like the nature of a beast. So be it.

Speaker: Red Lucy
Topic_Name: I'll defeat as many as you've got.
EN: Get to your cage and ready your arm.
